Source handlers maintained source files, polygraph schedules, and validation procedures to ensure source reliability and operational security throughout the source's reporting career.

TOC, Patrol Six. Spot report. One vehicle, technical-type, mounted heavy machine gun, observed at MSR Tampa, grid Mike-Romeo eight-eight-two-three-four-five. Vehicle is stationary, two PAX dismounted, posture unknown. Requesting permission to engage with organic assets or vector air. Stand by for further. Patrol Six, out.

Far ambush, direction nine o'clock, two hundred meters out. Vehicle commander calls actions on contact. Gunner returns fire on identified enemy positions. Driver maneuvers vehicle to maximize armor against the threat. Dismounts remain mounted, prepared to dismount on order. Spot report transmitted to platoon net. Maneuver to a covered position and assess. Decision points: break contact, assault through, or fix and report.

Service and support: maintenance teams are positioned at the assembly area with one wrecker on standby for vehicle recovery. Casualty evacuation flows through the company CCP, then to Role One at the battalion aid station. EPW handling per the FRAGO annex, search, silence, segregate, safeguard, speed, tag. All sensitive items inventoried before crossing the line of departure.

Quick-fire net connected the forward observers, the battalion fire direction center, and the firing batteries on a single push. The FO transmitted call for fire elements, the FDC computed firing data and pushed it to the battery, and the battery returned ready and shot reports. Total mission processing time from initial call to first round impact averaged under three minutes for well-trained battalions in field conditions.

On contact, immediately return fire, take cover, locate the enemy. Suppress the enemy with accurate fires. Maneuver to a position of advantage. Assault through the objective. Consolidate and reorganize. Report up to higher with size, activity, location, unit, time, and equipment of the enemy. These are the basic battle drills every infantryman must execute reflexively under stress.

Final defensive fires for the brigade defense were planned, registered, and pre-loaded as priority target one for each firing battery. When the FDC received the FPF call, every gun in range fired four rounds per minute at the planned grid coordinates. The volume of fire was designed to break up enemy assault formations within rifle range of the friendly main battle area. Crews drilled the procedure until it ran on instinct.

KLE preparation includes a review of the leader's biography, the prior engagement notes, the current operational situation in the leader's area, and the key messages to be conveyed. The engagement is rehearsed with the interpreter to ensure cultural nuance is preserved. Talking points are prioritized in case the meeting is shortened. Follow-up actions are identified in advance. The engagement is conducted with appropriate respect for local custom and the leader's status.

TOC discipline kept the operations bay focused on the fight. No unnecessary conversation, no cell phones, no eating at the workstations. The watch officer enforced the standard. Visitors checked in with the watch NCO and remained out of the workflow unless directly contributing to the operation. The TOC was a working space, not a meeting space, throughout the operation tempo.

MEDEVAC request, urgent. Line One: grid four-five-six-seven-eight-niner. Line Two: this freq, callsign Two-Six. Line Three: A is urgent, one patient, blast injury, both lower extremities, tourniquets in place. Line Four: none. Line Five: one litter. Line Six: Charlie, possible IDF in vicinity, recommend gunship escort. Line Seven: smoke on arrival, color last. Line Eight: alpha, US military. Line Nine: rocky, suitable hoist only.

Enemy course of action analysis produces the most likely and most dangerous COA, with sketches and narratives. Most likely COA represents the enemy's preferred approach based on doctrine, capability, and observed indicators. Most dangerous COA is what the enemy could do that would cause the greatest harm if executed. Both COAs are wargamed against friendly options to identify decision points and branches.

Convoy arrival at the destination requires occupy and secure procedures. Vehicles enter the perimeter in numerical order, park in dispersed configuration, dismounts establish local security. Manifest reconciliation by the trail vehicle commander. Sensitive items verified. Casualties processed through the aid station if any. Vehicle status report to higher. Drivers conduct post-operational checks. Maintenance reported to the FSC.

Order of march for the convoy is lead vehicle MRAP one-one, then HEMTT two-one through two-five carrying Class V, then HMMWV three-one, ambulance four-one in the middle, command vehicle five-one with the convoy commander, and trail MRAP six-one. Intervals adjusted based on threat level and terrain. Communications via FM secure, backup is hand and arm signals at halts.

Route classification by engineers includes width, surface, slope, restrictions such as overhead clearances, and any constraints requiring upgrade or repair. Routes are designated MSR, ASR, or restricted based on their suitability for sustained traffic. Daily route reports update the operations cell on the status of each designated route. Upgrade priorities are recommended to the commander based on operational impact. Engineer effort is allocated accordingly.

Raid is a limited objective operation with the purpose of seizing personnel, equipment, or intelligence, then withdrawing rapidly. Phases include planning, infiltration, actions on the objective, exfiltration. Planning requires detailed target package, IPB, route analysis, sustainment plan, and contingency development. Rehearsals occur at full mission profile when time permits, otherwise key tasks are walked through at minimum.

Sustainment posture is amber across the formation. Class I is green, sufficient for seventy-two hours. Class III amber, fuel consumption higher than projected due to extended sector. Class V amber, expended sixty percent of basic load during last engagement, resupply requested. Class IX red on Bradley track parts, prescribed load list inadequate for current operational tempo. Brief sustainment huddle at one-eight-hundred.

The armor battalion attacked along axis Brown with the lead company conducting movement to contact, the second company in echelon right for flank security, and the third company in reserve. Scout platoon screened forward two terrain features ahead of the lead company. Engineer obstacle reduction assets traveled with the lead company prepared to reduce obstacles in stride. The battalion commander tracked the fight from his vehicle near the company in contact.

The 81mm mortar section emplaced on the reverse slope behind the company position, registered base point one hundred meters in front of the trace, and recorded firing data on the gun cards. The section sergeant calculated final protective fires for the company defense and confirmed the FPF azimuth with the company commander. The crews stayed prepared to fire within ninety seconds of the call, regardless of weather or visibility.

All callsigns Echo on this push, conduct radio check by tac-org. Echo Six, Echo One-Six, Echo Two-Six, Echo Three-Six, Echo Four-Six in sequence. Standby. If you do not hear me when I call you, report immediately to NCS on backup frequency. Crypto roll is at one-eight-hundred, fills on hand at each station before sundown.

Key terrain in counterinsurgency operations was human terrain rather than physical terrain. The insurgent network drew strength from population support, financial flows, ideological appeal, and external safe havens. Counterinsurgency targeted each of these sources of insurgent strength simultaneously through kinetic, information, civil, and intelligence operations. Patience characterized successful campaigns; impatience characterized failed ones across the conflict zones the brigade had studied.

The military information support operations detachment supported the joint task force with strategic, operational, and tactical capabilities. Strategic products targeted regional populations with long-term messaging. Operational products targeted opposing decision-makers with deception or deterrent messaging. Tactical products supported maneuver units with immediate effects on enemy combat forces. Each level required different approval authorities and synchronization mechanisms.

Friendly aircraft on station, callsign Hawg One-Two, type Alpha-One-Zero. Frequency Uniform-Hotel-Foxtrot pre-set channel four. IFF squawking Mode Three correct. Visual identification, single ship, low and west. Friendly mark with VS-17 panel orange side up, supplemented by Sierra-Bravo for night identification. Acknowledge.

Hasty attack exploited a window of opportunity before the enemy could prepare a defense. The lead element bypassed light resistance, fixed the main enemy position, and called the main effort forward for the assault. Hasty attacks traded planning depth for speed of execution. Junior leaders made on-the-spot decisions about the scheme of maneuver while the higher headquarters generated supporting effects through fires, intelligence, and sustainment.

Synchronization matrix integrates time-phased events across warfighting functions to ensure all actions reinforce the commander's intent. Rows are organized by warfighting function: intelligence, movement and maneuver, fires, protection, sustainment, command and control. Columns are time phases or named events. The matrix is the primary product of the wargame and is briefed at the OPORD. Updates flow through the FRAGO process during execution.

Positive identification standard requires reasonable certainty that the proposed target is a legitimate military objective. This is a higher standard than mere suspicion. Indicators include observed weapons, hostile actions, communications intercepts properly authorized, and pattern of life consistent with combatant activity. PID is documented in the after-action report along with the engagement decision rationale.

Detainee handling at the checkpoint followed five-S procedures: search, silence, segregate, safeguard, and speed to the rear. Each detained individual received tactical questioning to gather time-sensitive intelligence, was photographed and biometrically enrolled, and was processed for transfer to the brigade detention facility. Documentation captured the basis for detention to support subsequent legal review. Detainee operations balanced intelligence value against legal and ethical requirements throughout processing.

Forward arming and refueling points supported aviation operations beyond the helicopter base. Each FARP positioned to extend rotary wing range, support multiple lift operations, and refuel and rearm aircraft on the ground in minimum time. The FARP crew conducted hot refueling with rotors turning, loaded ammunition under expedited procedures, and dispatched aircraft back to mission within fifteen minutes of arrival at the FARP. Aviation tempo demanded FARP efficiency throughout sustained operations.

I spell the grid for you. Hotel, India, Delta, Echo, break. Then numerics six, eight, four, two, five, niner. Read back. Negative, my last, second letter is India not Indigo, third is Delta not Dakota. Use standard phonetic only. Confirm correct grid before plotting. Over.

Reconnaissance handoff is conducted when one scout element relieves another at an OP or NAI. Handoff procedures include passing of map graphics, logs, sketches, and any equipment in place. Verbal brief covers observed patterns, enemy activity, friendly forces in the area, and the supported unit's information requirements. Outgoing element confirms the relieving element has full situational awareness before departing. Continuity of observation is maintained throughout the handoff.

Trigger lines along the engagement area cued indirect fires, obstacle activation, and direct fire engagement at specific ranges from the friendly position. The S3 designated each trigger line with corresponding tasks and reporting requirements. Observers positioned to view each trigger line, identified enemy crossing the line, and called the associated actions. Sequential trigger lines built the engagement from disruption at long range to destruction at close range.

Drill seven covers entering and clearing a trench. The lead element threw a frag, called frag out, and rolled into the trench with weapons at the high ready. Subsequent soldiers stacked behind and bounded forward, clearing each bend and intersection. The trail squad set in security at the entry point and prepared to receive casualties or pass forward additional ammunition. The company XO timed the clear from initial entry to consolidation and signoff.

Key leader engagement schedules required the civil affairs team to maintain relationships with local elders, religious leaders, business figures, and government officials. Each engagement built rapport, gathered atmospherics, identified emerging issues, and reinforced friendly intent in the area. The team prepared talking points before each engagement and produced contact reports afterward for the brigade S2 and the CMOC database.

Response force operations in the rear area provided rapid reaction to enemy actions or other incidents behind friendly lines. The response force maintained alert status, rehearsed multiple contingency response scenarios, and tracked friendly and enemy activity throughout the rear area. Response time to any point within the area of operations was tracked as a force readiness metric. Quick reaction time minimized enemy success against vulnerable rear area targets.

Course of action analysis war-gamed the friendly COAs against the most likely enemy COA and the most dangerous enemy COA. The staff used the action-reaction-counteraction method to project how the operation would unfold turn by turn. The S2 played the enemy commander, the S3 maneuvered friendly forces, and supporting staff officers tracked their warfighting function impacts. The war game identified branches, sequels, and decision points requiring further planning.

End of mission, MEDEVAC complete. Patient handed over to flight medic at one-three-four-five local. Casualty card and TCCC card transferred with the patient. LZ closed, panel and smoke recovered. Element collapsing back to assembly area. Higher notified of patient destination and condition. Out.

Crossing area headquarters controlled traffic at the bridge site to maximize throughput while maintaining security. Each unit cleared the crossing in serial order with strict timing to prevent congestion on either bank. Military police provided traffic control points; air defense provided cover against rotary wing threats; and the brigade reserve stood ready to reinforce the bridgehead if the enemy counterattacked the crossing operation.

Direct fire planning at the company level integrates each weapon system into a coherent engagement plan. Sectors of fire are assigned to each crew-served weapon. Engagement areas are developed to canalize and destroy enemy formations. Trigger lines and TRPs are designated to initiate massed fires at decisive moments. The fire plan is rehearsed and tested with dry runs prior to enemy contact. Adjustments are made based on rehearsal findings.

Battery, fire mission, area target. Center of mass grid romeo-papa three-four-five-six-seven-eight. Length four hundred, width two hundred, attitude one-six-zero-zero mils. Enemy mortar position, low priority danger close to friendly element on western flank. Method, two volleys, time on target one-four-three-zero. ICM in effect, then DPICM follow-on. Stand by, fire for effect on my command.

Fire command sequence per doctrine: alert, target, weapons or ammunition, direction, range, method of engagement, control. Example: 'Squad, frontal, machine gun, twelve o'clock, two hundred meters, fire at my command, ready, fire'. The sequence is brief, complete, and unambiguous. Each element conveys necessary information to crews. Adjustments and corrections follow the same format. Repetition for clarity is permitted but conciseness is preferred under stress.

Combined arms training centers ran multinational exercises to validate coalition interoperability before operational employment. Exercises tested communications interoperability, common procedures, doctrinal alignment, and unified action across national contingents. Lessons learned drove refinements to standard operating procedures and tactics, techniques, and procedures that bridged national doctrinal differences. The exercises built professional relationships among coalition military leaders.

Obstacle zones, belts, and groups followed a hierarchical structure that connected the corps engineer plan to the company engineer effort. The corps designated obstacle zones; the division designated obstacle belts within zones; the brigade designated obstacle groups within belts; and the battalion emplaced individual obstacles within groups. The hierarchy ensured every obstacle supported a higher-echelon scheme of maneuver and obstacle effort.

Engineer reconnaissance precedes the maneuver force to identify obstacles, mobility corridors, and route conditions. Engineers report bridge classifications using military load class, road conditions using surface type and width, and any obstacles by type, dimensions, and likely emplacement effort. Information feeds the operations cell's planning and the route designation process. Recon engineers also identify locations suitable for assembly areas, command posts, and logistical sites.

Operations, this is the company commander. Personnel status: ninety-six out of one hundred and twelve, four on quarters. Equipment readiness: vehicles green, comms green, NVGs amber pending fresh batteries on the LOGPAC. Training: company conducted live fire reflexive engagement, all squads passed. No Class A incidents this reporting period. Will brief BC at the eighteen hundred huddle. Over.

Class IX repair parts shortage has created cascading deadlines across the formation. Authorized stockage list at the BSA is being expedited through the SARSS system. Critical low density items including track shoes, road wheels, and engine assemblies are on backorder from the wholesale level. Recommend the commander engage at the next sustainment huddle to push priority back to division G-4.

Short-range air defense Avenger sections provided point defense for high-value assets across the brigade footprint. Stinger missiles engaged rotary wing and slow-moving fixed wing threats out to four kilometers. The section sergeant positioned launchers to maximize engagement geometry against likely threat axes. Sector sketches captured fields of fire, dead space, and tied-in coverage with adjacent sections. Coverage gaps received supplemental coverage from organic small arms air defense fires.

Movement to contact began when the enemy situation lacked sufficient clarity to develop a deliberate attack plan. Lead elements moved aggressively to develop the situation through contact, gathered information through engagement, and reported the enemy disposition to higher headquarters. The brigade commander developed his attack plan based on contact reports while the lead elements continued to find, fix, and identify the enemy main body and supporting positions.

Weapons control status governed air defense engagement authority across the operation. Weapons free permitted engagement of any aircraft not positively identified as friendly. Weapons tight required positive identification before engagement. Weapons hold prohibited all engagement except in self-defense. The area air defense commander adjusted weapons control status across the AOR based on the air threat, friendly air operations tempo, and risk to friendly aviation from inadvertent engagement.

Area of operations transfer between units required deliberate battle handover procedures. The relieving unit's reconnaissance preceded the main body to receive the situation from the outgoing unit. Battle handover line marked the seam between forces during the transition. Once the relief in place was complete and the new commander assumed battlespace ownership, the outgoing unit moved to its next mission or returned to garrison.

Sniper school taught ballistics, optics, range estimation, and stalking, but the heart of the course was decision making under time pressure. The candidate had to read the situation, identify the target, calculate the firing solution, and execute the shot within seconds, sometimes from awkward positions and under simulated stress. The shooter who could maintain his fundamentals when his heart rate spiked was the shooter who passed.

Map boards along the TOC walls displayed the brigade graphics, the enemy situation overlay, the fire support plan, the engineer obstacle plan, and the sustainment overlay. Staff officers updated their respective overlays with grease pencil annotations as the situation changed. The maps provided redundancy against digital system failures and visual reference points for the commander and staff during decision discussions.

Random antiterrorism measures this week include irregular vehicle inspection patterns at ECP One, dismounted patrols varied by route and timing through the housing area, and unscheduled credential checks at the dining facility entrance. Purpose is to disrupt potential surveillance patterns and present an unpredictable security profile to any hostile observer. RAM matrix is classified at the unit level. Brief the cycle weekly at the security working group.

Live fire exercises validated unit collective tasks under realistic conditions with live ammunition. Range safety officers controlled the exercise to prevent accidents while preserving training value. Each iteration progressed from walk-through to dry fire to blank fire to live fire with increasing complexity. The company first sergeant tracked ammunition issue, accountability, and turn-in throughout the exercise to maintain control of munitions on the range complex during training operations.

Joint targeting prioritization placed high-value targets, high-payoff targets, and time-sensitive targets in distinct categories for collection and engagement. The joint targeting working group reviewed nominations against the commander's targeting guidance and validated each through the targeting cycle. Time-sensitive targets bypassed the normal cycle for immediate engagement when target perishability and military value warranted accelerated processing.

Special operations sustainment functioned outside normal supply channels through dedicated sustainment elements supporting deployed teams. Each operational detachment received tailored sustainment packages reflecting mission duration, environmental conditions, and resupply opportunities. Forward operating bases supporting special operations maintained specialized inventories including foreign weapons ammunition, partner force equipment, and mission-specific items not commonly stocked. Sustainment innovation enabled operational flexibility across diverse mission profiles.

Triangular patrol base configuration provides three-sixty coverage with crew-served weapons or automatic weapons at each apex. Interior is reserved for the patrol leader's CP, the medic position, and the consolidation point. Listening posts are emplaced fifty to one hundred meters forward of each apex, rotating every two to four hours. Internal communication is wire if available, otherwise hand signals.

MOPP level four is the highest mission-oriented protective posture, requiring suit, mask, gloves, and overboots. Personnel in MOPP four experience significant physical degradation, including reduced visibility, heat stress, communications difficulty, and impaired fine motor function. Work-rest cycles are managed by the chain of command, with frequent rotation, hydration, and cooling. Mission-essential tasks are prioritized, non-essential activities deferred until downgrade.

Loudspeaker operations from the tactical PSYOP detachment encouraged enemy surrender during the cordon operation. The team broadcast in the local language from a safe distance, identified themselves, described the situation, offered terms for surrender, and provided procedures for safe handover. Tactical commanders integrated the broadcasts with maneuver to maximize psychological pressure on isolated enemy elements.

Action at the short halt: vehicles stop in herringbone formation, alternating to opposite sides of the road, weapons oriented outboard. Gunners scan for threats. Drivers remain at the wheel. Dismounts dismount only on order. Halts under ten minutes. Long halts require local security with dismount teams pushing out to three-sixty coverage. Convoy commander walks the line and checks each vehicle.

Bounding overwatch between tank sections kept continuous fires on suspected enemy positions during the movement to contact. Alpha section took the high ground, oriented weapons forward, and called Bravo section forward bound by bound. The platoon leader coordinated with the scout platoon to his front and the mechanized infantry company to his flank. Tank-infantry team coordination prevented bypass and supported each other through close terrain.

Collateral damage estimation methodology requires identification of the weapon system, the target type, the proximity of noncombatants, and the assessed precision of the engagement. CDE level determines required approval authority for the strike. CDE Five requires combatant command approval. Lower CDE levels can be delegated to subordinate echelons. Failure to follow CDE procedures may result in a credible incident investigation.

Patrol leader gave the contact left hand-and-arm signal. Squad executed the immediate action drill, suppressing element returned fire while the maneuver element broke contact to the south. Once disengaged, the patrol consolidated at rally point Bravo. Accountability check, all PAX present. Combat ineffective casualties were zero. Patrol leader called in spot report to higher and requested permission to break contact further.

Performance versus effectiveness distinction is critical to honest assessment. A unit can be performing every task to standard while still failing to achieve the desired effect. This often indicates a faulty operational concept rather than a lack of effort. The assessment process must surface such disconnects and feed them back into planning. Commanders who reward performance without examining effectiveness can find themselves successfully executing the wrong strategy.

Stalking exercise required movement from the start line to within two hundred meters of the observer post without detection while taking two qualifying shots. The students crawled through the high grass for six hours, controlling movement, avoiding skyline silhouettes, and using available concealment. Only two of the eight candidates qualified on the first attempt. The rest cycled back for additional reps until they could meet the standard.

Escalation of force procedures at the checkpoint progressed from visible presence to verbal warnings, hand signals, warning shots, disabling shots, and finally deadly force engagement. Each step gave the approaching driver opportunity to comply with checkpoint directions. The platoon documented each escalation event with sworn statements and photographic evidence. Most drivers complied at the verbal warning stage and proceeded through the search lane without further escalation.

Succession of command is rehearsed and documented at every level. Primary, alternate, contingency, and emergency commanders are designated. PACE plan for command and control communications is published and rehearsed. Loss of commander or key leader is treated as an immediate event triggering the succession protocol. The new commander or leader assumes responsibility, issues a positional FRAGO, and reports up the chain on the succession event.

Mortuary affairs collection point is co-located with the medical aid station at the BSA. Procedures for handling remains are per regulation, with chain of custody documentation maintained by the mortuary affairs NCO. Personal effects are bagged and tagged separately. Coordination with the casualty assistance officer at higher headquarters is required prior to onward movement of remains to theater mortuary.

Obstacle plan integrates barriers, minefields, and demolitions into the defensive scheme. Each obstacle has a purpose: disrupt, turn, fix, or block enemy movement. Obstacles are covered by fire to be effective. Reserve demolitions are pre-prepared and executed on order at specific events. Obstacle status reporting, including emplacement progress, completion, and arming, is provided to the operations cell. Records of all emplaced obstacles are maintained for eventual recovery or transfer.

Type 1 control requires the JTAC to visually acquire both the attacking aircraft and the target. Type 2 control requires JTAC to visually acquire the target or to confirm target via other means but not necessarily the aircraft. Type 3 control permits multiple attacks against the same target area without individual clearance for each pass. Selection depends on weather, terrain, and risk to friendly forces.

Selection criteria for patrol base location include cover and concealment, drainage, defensibility, dispersion potential, away from known human and animal trails, away from natural lines of drift, and sufficient distance from likely enemy avenues of approach. Avoid hilltops, ridgelines, and topographic features that are obvious to the enemy. Patrol base is occupied no longer than twenty-four hours.

Excalibur precision-guided munitions extended artillery accuracy to within four meters of the aim point at maximum range. The forward observer designated the target with a laser, the round received GPS coordinates in flight, and impact tolerances allowed engagement near friendly forces with minimal risk. Precision fires changed the targeting calculus by enabling engagement of point targets that previously required close air support or maneuver assault.

MEDEVAC requested for two urgent surgical, one priority, and three routine casualties at grid Whiskey Bravo two-four-zero-zero-eight-five-zero-zero. The platoon medic transmitted the nine-line, the company first sergeant marked the pickup zone with VS-17 panels, and the air ambulance lifted from the forward arming and refueling point. Time from request to wheels-up was under eight minutes. The Black Hawk medics provided en route care during the twelve-minute flight to the role two facility.

Hide site discipline kept the team operational through three days on station. No skylined silhouettes, no reflective surfaces, no sudden movements, no ambient noise. The team operated on a sleep rotation with one observer always alert behind the spotting scope. Trash was bagged and carried out at extraction; human waste went into double bags. The site discipline left no signature when the team broke down and exfiltrated to the linkup point.

The CA team integrated with the maneuver company during cordon and search operations to manage civilian populations affected by the operation. Civilians displaced from search sites went to a designated holding area where the team provided basic needs, gathered information, and coordinated return to homes once the operation concluded. Civilian sensitivity throughout the operation supported the broader counterinsurgency line of effort.

Armed unmanned aircraft systems extended brigade strike capability with persistent overwatch and precision engagement. The Gray Eagle carried Hellfire missiles, conducted twenty-four-hour overwatch missions, and could engage time-sensitive targets within the rules of engagement. The mission commander coordinated strike authorities through the brigade fire support cell. Each engagement followed positive identification, collateral damage estimate, and approval procedures before weapons release authorized.

Crew-served weapon emplacement requires proper site selection: defilade where possible to protect the crew, primary and alternate positions, supplemental positions to cover unexpected enemy avenues, dead space identification within sector, and primary and grazing fires planning. Overhead cover and fighting position improvement are critical. Crews dig in to the standard prescribed in the unit SOP, with revetment, drainage, and field of fire clearance.

Exercise control has called administrative freeze for one-five mikes to reposition observer-controllers. BLUEFOR and REDFOR commanders will remain in current locations. No movement on either side, no fires, no comms traffic except admin. Resumption signal will be three flares, green, on the master grid. Use this time to consolidate logs and prepare for AAR. Out.

Direct action missions by special operations forces struck high-value targets through precise raids, ambushes, and recovery operations. The mission planning cycle compressed deliberate planning into hours rather than days when intelligence indicated time-sensitive opportunities. Mission rehearsal of concept drills validated each operator's actions on the objective. The strike force infiltrated, executed actions on objective, exfiltrated, and conducted sensitive site exploitation against captured material throughout the operation.

Reaction to indirect fire. First round splash, identify direction and adjust posture. Disperse, take cover behind hardened terrain or hardened vehicles. Mark POO if possible through observation of dust, sound, or flash. Pass counter-battery grid to higher for FA mission. Account for personnel. Do not bunch up. Continue mission only after the threat is suppressed or shifted. Maintain noise and light discipline if moving.

Threat update has elevated FPCON to Charlie based on credible reporting. All personnel are confined to garrison. Off-post travel is suspended pending further notice. ECP procedures are heightened, all vehicles searched on entry, occupants identified and credentials verified. Crew-served weapon positions are manned continuously. Random anti-terrorism measures are doubled in frequency. Brief all personnel at the morning huddle.

Command relationships in the operations order specified the authorities and responsibilities of each subordinate unit. Operational control gave the commander authority over assigned forces for missions limited in nature, time, location, or function. Tactical control gave authority for local direction of movements and maneuvers necessary to accomplish missions or tasks assigned. Administrative control retained service responsibilities including administration, training, and logistics through the parent unit chain.

End of training day, BLUEFOR brigade is at REDCON-3, REDFOR motorized regiment at REDCON-2 pending overnight reset. Both sides will conduct standdown actions, weapons cleared, vehicles into the maintenance posture, leadership huddle for the daily AAR at the BDOC. Exercise will resume at zero-six-hundred local with the FRAGO already disseminated. OC/T cell will be on call overnight.

Mass casualty incidents required deliberate procedures to manage simultaneous treatment and evacuation of more casualties than the organic medical assets could handle. The senior medic assumed control of the casualty collection point, conducted START triage, requested additional MEDEVAC platforms, and coordinated with the brigade surgeon for evacuation priorities. Mass casualty plans rehearsed in advance saved minutes that translated directly to lives saved during actual incidents.

Reaction to ambush is to push through the kill zone if possible. Vehicles do not stop in the kill zone. Gunners return fire on identified threats. Damaged vehicles are pushed by trail vehicles or recovered later. Casualties are extracted at the safe area beyond the kill zone. Convoy commander reports up immediately with grid, size of attacking force, casualties, and damage. Higher provides QRF as available.

Radiological survey teams conduct dose-rate measurements at predetermined locations within and around the suspected contaminated area. Readings are plotted on the overlay and used to calculate isodose lines. Total dose calculations are made for personnel based on time in contaminated areas. Operational exposure guidance is briefed to commanders to support risk decisions. Dosimeters are issued and read daily during operations in contaminated environments.

Survivability position construction follows specifications by occupant type and threat level. Crew-served weapon positions include parapets, elevated firing positions, and overhead cover. Vehicle fighting positions allow turret defilade and hull defilade. Command post positions provide reinforced overhead cover against indirect fire. Construction times are estimated for planning and tracked during execution. Spoil management prevents enemy observation. Camouflage is applied as positions are constructed.

The electronic warfare officer coordinated electronic attack, electronic support, and electronic protection across the brigade operational area. The EW cell tasked organic and joint EW capabilities against enemy command and control, navigation, and communications. Each engagement required deconfliction with friendly electromagnetic emissions, signal intelligence collection requirements, and authorized release procedures. EW operations contested the electromagnetic spectrum as a domain of operations rather than a supporting function.

Sleep plan in the patrol base allocates four hours per soldier across a twelve-hour cycle. One-third remains on security at all times. Squad leaders rotate by sector, ensuring overlapping coverage during transitions. Patrol leader and platoon sergeant maintain awareness of the cycle and adjust based on threat level. Sleep is permitted only in designated locations within the perimeter, weapon in hand.

Indirect fire alarm has sounded. All personnel take cover in the nearest hardened structure or bunker. Accountability will be conducted by chain of command within five mikes of all-clear. Counter-battery radar acquired the point of origin and has passed grid to fires. Counter-battery mission is in flight. Stand fast until further direction from the BDOC.

Joint targeting cycle followed deliberate steps from commander's intent through target development, weaponeering, target list management, and assessment. The joint integrated prioritized target list captured high-payoff targets requiring joint capabilities to engage. The collateral damage estimate process validated each strike against ROE and the commander's risk tolerance. Targeting boards convened daily to refine priorities and approve strikes.

Steel Six-Four, this is Observer Two-One. Fire mission, polar. Direction two-eight-four-zero mils, distance one-two-hundred, dropping fifty. Target description: enemy squad in the open, danger close. Request high explosive in effect, point detonating. Three rounds, fire for effect. Method of fire and control, at my command. Over.

Departure of the patrol base requires a leader's recon of the planned route, security elements posted at the release point, and a head count and sensitive items check before stepping off. Light and noise discipline are absolute. Last action before departure is to sterilize the position: police all trash, fill in hasty fighting positions if time permits, recover all wire and pyrotechnics.

Geospatial intelligence products supported the brigade with high-resolution imagery, terrain analysis, and predictive line-of-sight calculations across the AOR. The GEOINT cell produced products on demand: mission planning maps, fortification analysis, route reconnaissance, and battle damage assessment imagery. Reach-back to the national geospatial intelligence agency provided products beyond organic GEOINT cell capabilities. Imagery analysis informed every phase of the planning and execution cycle.

Event template synthesizes the threat COA, the terrain analysis, and the friendly scheme of maneuver into a single product that depicts where and when key enemy actions are expected to occur. Decision points for the commander are tied to specific events on the template. The collection plan is keyed to the event template, ensuring assets are positioned to observe critical indicators in time to inform decisions.

MILES casualty cards collected from the lane reflect a BLUEFOR to REDFOR loss ratio of three to one, unfavorable for the attacker. After action review will focus on actions on the objective, particularly consolidation and reorganization, where BLUEFOR was caught by REDFOR's local counterattack while still in the disorganized phase. Lessons learned to be integrated into the next training cycle.

Mobility, countermobility, and survivability are the three core engineer functions. Mobility tasks remove obstacles and enable friendly movement. Countermobility tasks emplace obstacles to slow, divert, or destroy enemy movement. Survivability tasks construct fighting positions and fortifications. Each function requires specific equipment, training, and time. The engineer commander balances the three based on the supported unit's priorities and the operational situation.

All stations, this net, SITREP at zero-six-hundred local. BLUEFOR has consolidated on Phase Line Tango. REDFOR appears to be repositioning to the north, likely a forward passage of lines. Combat power assessed at eighty-five percent. CL III and CL V resupply expected by LOGPAC at twelve hundred. Continue current task and purpose until further FRAGO. How copy, over.

Paragraph four, sustainment. Logistics: Class I, three days MRE on the man, water resupply by LOGPAC at phase line Bravo. Class III not required for this dismounted operation. Class V, basic load plus one bandolier per rifleman, double basic on grenades. Class VIII, combat lifesaver bag at squad level, aid station co-located with company TOC.

Counter-IED procedures for the convoy include EOD sweep of the route prior to departure where feasible, route reconnaissance overflight when available, varied departure times, and randomized routing within the planned scheme. Vehicle commanders scan for known IED indicators: disturbed earth, debris piles, command wires, suspicious dismounts on the route. Distance to potential threats is the primary mitigation.

Forward observer to FDC, request final protective fires on FPF Echo. Direction one-six-zero-zero mils. Enemy attempting to breach our wire. Continuous illumination on TRP One, sustained until further orders. We are pinned in our primary fighting positions. Confirm FPF rounds outbound. Acknowledge time of flight. Over, urgent.

Bomb suit operations require extensive training and physical conditioning. The suit weighs over thirty kilograms and significantly degrades mobility, dexterity, and field of view. EOD technicians work in pairs with a controller in the safe area monitoring vitals and communications. Operations in the suit are kept brief, typically under thirty minutes per session. Cooling vests and hydration are essential particularly in hot environments.

The beachhead expanded inland to the force beachhead line by H-plus-six hours. Battalions cleared their assigned zones, established blocking positions on key avenues of approach, and prepared to receive follow-on forces through the lodgement. The MEU commander assessed the situation and either committed the helicopter-borne reserve, expanded the lodgement, or transitioned to follow-on operations as conditions permitted.

Combat configured load for the tank included thirty rounds of sabot, ten rounds of HEAT, and ten rounds of canister or multi-purpose ammunition depending on the threat assessment. Coaxial machine gun ammunition stowed in the turret; .50 cal ammunition for the commander's weapon in the loader's position. The loader controlled ammunition flow during engagement and called out the round type as he indexed each main gun round.

Anti-terrorism officer has reviewed the FOB layout and identified vulnerabilities at ECP Three, where the serpentine is insufficient to defeat a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device traveling at moderate speed. Recommend installation of additional T-walls and a Jersey barrier emplacement at the speed-bump line. Mitigation must be in place within forty-eight hours. Status reports to the commander every twelve hours until complete.

Final protective fires for the company were planned along the most dangerous avenue of approach, registered before EENT, and stored as priority target one. If the platoon called for FPF, the mortars fired four rounds per tube per minute until the threat broke contact or the company commander called the fires off. FPF could break up a dismounted assault before it closed within hand grenade range of the defensive position.

Combat cargo loading aboard the LSD followed a unit deployment list that prioritized fight-on-arrival capability. Vehicles, ammunition, and fuel loaded first into the well deck and vehicle stowage spaces. Sustainment cargo loaded into the upper decks for follow-on offload after the beachhead was established. The combat cargo officer maintained the load plan and adjusted for any last-minute changes in the embarkation order.

Knowledge management at the headquarters captures, organizes, and disseminates information needed for decision making. Shared portals, structured collaboration spaces, and standardized briefing formats reduce friction. The knowledge management officer maintains the staff battle rhythm calendar, the running estimates, and the after-action review files. New personnel are integrated through a structured onboarding process. Information overload is mitigated by ruthless prioritization.

The MLRS battery received the fire mission via the digital fire control system, validated the target against the airspace control measures, calculated launcher orientation, and engaged the target with a single launcher load of six rockets at zero plus thirty seconds from mission receipt. The launcher displaced immediately after firing to evade counter-battery acquisition. Shoot and scoot tactics preserved the battery's survival on a contested battlefield.

Doc Six, this is Hotel Two-Three Echo. Requesting MEDEVAC. Nine-line follows. Pickup site is grid romeo-bravo two-seven-five-three-eight-one. Three patients, one Cat A gunshot wound to chest, sucking chest wound treated with occlusive dressing. Two Cat B fragmentation wounds, ambulatory. LZ is secure, marked with red smoke at time of arrival. Send aircraft on direct, ETA priority for the Cat A. Over.

Convoy AAR conducted within thirty minutes of arrival. Topics covered include route observations, threats encountered, lessons learned on actions on contact, comms performance, vehicle performance, and recommendations for the next iteration. Inputs feed the lessons learned database at the BSA. Vehicle commanders document significant events in the daily log. Convoy commander signs the trip ticket and files the after-action.

The brigade attacked along axis Gold toward objective Cougar with one battalion in the main effort, one in supporting effort, and one in reserve. The attack began at zero-four-thirty with shaping fires on enemy positions, breach operations through the obstacle belt, and movement to contact along the assault avenue. The brigade commander synchronized the attack from his tactical command post forward of the brigade trains.

Hostile act is defined as an attack or other use of force against US forces or other designated persons and property. Hostile intent is the threat of imminent use of force. Both standards justify the use of proportional force in self-defense, but commanders should document the articulable indicators that led to the determination. Legal review post-engagement is standard practice.

Beach landing site Alpha was designated by the Marine expeditionary unit commander after detailed beach reconnaissance by the reconnaissance battalion. Surf zone conditions, beach gradient, exit routes, and enemy coastal defense positions all factored into the selection. Wave one carried the assault companies, wave two the heavy weapons and command element, and subsequent waves brought sustainment and combat support.

React to indirect fire drill required immediate dispersion, accountability check, and movement out of the impact area along a pre-planned azimuth. The platoon practiced it at every halt during the exercise. The platoon sergeant kept a notebook of times and called out anyone slow to move. By day three, the drill ran under fifteen seconds from first round impact to dispersed defensive posture.

Family of scatterable mines provided air-delivered, artillery-delivered, and ground-emplaced minefield capabilities. Each system delivered different mine types with different self-destruct times. The brigade obstacle planner selected the appropriate system based on emplacement timeline, expected enemy contact, and the duration the obstacle needed to remain effective. Self-destruct features prevented long-term hazards to civilians and friendly forces after operations concluded.

Observation post emplacement criteria: cover and concealment from likely enemy avenues of observation, fields of observation across the entire NAI, defensible position with covered withdrawal route, communications connectivity with higher, and absence of known enemy patrol patterns. OPs are typically two-man positions, rotated every twelve hours, supported by a patrol base in depth. Sectors of observation are formally assigned, with logs maintained throughout occupation.

Paragraph five, command and signal. Command, succession of command is platoon leader, platoon sergeant, first squad leader. Higher commander is at company TOC, callsign Mike Six. Signal, primary is FM secure freq Alpha, alternate is FM secure freq Bravo, contingency is line of sight, emergency is signal mirror or smoke. Code words and challenge-pass per signal annex.

Rear area security operations protected lines of communication, sustainment facilities, and command and control nodes against threats up to and including conventional ground forces. The rear area operations center coordinated response forces, tracked enemy activity behind friendly lines, and managed force protection posture across the rear area. Levels of response progressed from local security to dedicated response forces to reinforcement by tactical combat forces drawn from the maneuver brigades.

EOD team responding to suspected IED at grid mike-romeo eight-eight-four-three-two-one. Initial assessment from the patrol element is a buried command-wire device, partially exposed. EOD team has set up the standoff at three hundred meters and is conducting a robot-mounted reconnaissance. Render safe procedures to follow once the device is positively characterized. Cordon is in place. EOD will brief the supported unit on the disposition of the device.

Hipshoot drill engaged targets of opportunity without prepared firing data. The gun crew lifted the tube out of the baseplate, set it on a suitable surface, oriented it by compass on the target azimuth, and dropped a single ranging round. The FO observed and adjusted, and the gun fired for effect once the adjustment was made. Hipshoot was emergency procedure when no other fires were available within engagement timelines.

No weapons visible. Recommend continued observation, requesting no engagement at this time. Will continue to track and report. Three-Six, out.

The team conducted a leader's recon of the proposed FFP at last light, confirmed line of sight to the target reference points, marked range card data for each likely engagement area, and returned to the patrol base before EENT. At zero-two-hundred the team moved to occupy the position, established communications with higher on the primary and alternate frequencies, and waited for first light to confirm the situation in the AO.

Convoy designation is Lima-Papa Two-Seven, all stations acknowledge by element. Lead vehicle is Lima-Papa Two-Seven Alpha. Trail vehicle is Lima-Papa Two-Seven Bravo. Casualty collection point in the convoy is the third vehicle, designated Charlie. Communications check at start point, ten minutes prior to roll. Use phonetic letters only on the net, no abbreviations.

Partnered operations with host nation security forces transitioned counterinsurgency responsibility over time. The brigade embedded military transition teams with host nation units, conducted partnered patrols, and gradually transferred lead for operations in the AOR. Each partnership built the host nation force's tactical, leadership, and sustainment capacity. Transition timelines depended on the host nation force's progress rather than coalition operational schedules. Patient capacity building preceded successful handover of security responsibility.

Sniper employment doctrine calls for overwatch of dismounted maneuver elements, counter-sniper operations, and reconnaissance in depth. The team operates beyond the FLOT with minimum communications, maximum stealth, and stand-off precision engagement capability. Battle handover with the supported unit happens through the S3 with established passage points and recognition signals to prevent fratricide.

Guns up, ready to fire. Charge four, white bag. Fuze quick. Deflection three-two-four-eight, quadrant three-six-five. Time of flight three-six seconds. Shot, out. Splash in zero-five. Forward observer, this is Fire Direction Center, all rounds complete, awaiting your battle damage assessment. Stand by for next mission. Out.

Pattern of life analysis tracked enemy behavior over time to identify routine activities, key personalities, and operational patterns. The intelligence analyst correlated reports from multiple collection disciplines to build a multidimensional picture of the target network. Disrupting enemy patterns of life forced the network to expose itself in unfamiliar ways, generating new collection opportunities. Patient analysis over weeks or months produced operational opportunities that rushed analysis missed.

The mortar platoon supported the rifle company throughout the operation with on-call and scheduled fires. Scheduled fires hit pre-planned targets at specific times to support the scheme of maneuver. On-call fires responded to emerging targets identified by the forward observers or the company commander. The fire support officer at the company maintained the synchronization between maneuver and fires through the company net.

Detention authority under the current ROE permits temporary detention of individuals assessed as posing a threat to the force or as having intelligence value. Detainees must be treated humanely. Five S's apply: search, silence, segregate, safeguard, speed. Tag with date, time, place of capture, capturing unit. Process through the detainee holding area within seventy-two hours.

Target package for the raid is developed by the S-2 in coordination with the operations cell. Contents include intelligence summary, imagery of the objective, named graphics, pattern of life summary, link analysis of associated personnel, structures floor plans where available, and likely enemy reaction templates. Target package is briefed at the OPORD and updated as new intelligence is received prior to execution.

Measures of performance assess whether a task was completed correctly and on time. MOPs answer 'are we doing things right'. Example MOPs for a deliberate attack include time from line of departure to objective, percentage of friendly losses, number of enemy positions cleared. MOPs are quantitative and observable. Each MOP is tied to a task and standard. Failure to meet a MOP triggers review of the execution.

The lift carried thirty soldiers per chalk in three Black Hawks. Total lift required three turns to insert the rifle company plus the heavy weapons section. Each turn took thirty-eight minutes round trip from PZ to LZ to refuel point. The S3 calculated total movement time, locked the SP and ROZ times, and built a synchronization matrix that tracked aircraft, ground force, and supporting fires through execution.

Rule of law operations supported host nation justice institutions through training prosecutors, judges, and corrections officials. Each component of the justice system needed parallel development to function: police investigations led to prosecution, prosecution led to trials, trials led to incarceration of convicted criminals. Gaps in any component undermined the entire chain. Justice sector development required years of patient capacity building beyond initial security operations conducted by the brigade.

Mortar section, fire mission, grid mission. Target description: enemy mortar baseplate suspected vicinity grid hotel-juliet four-five-six-seven-eight-niner. Two tubes, four rounds high explosive each. At my command. Smoke screen to follow on order, two rounds, two-hundred meters west of target, to cover maneuver element withdrawal back to the rally point. Confirm.

The tank platoon occupied a battle position oriented east with sectors of fire interlocking with the adjacent platoon. Each tank was set in a hull-down position with overhead concealment and routes to alternate and subsequent positions identified. The platoon leader's tank covered the primary engagement area; the wingman tank covered the secondary; the trail section maintained rear security against bypass.

Wedge formation provides three-sixty degree security and good control for the squad leader. Squad leader is at the apex, fire team leaders are positioned to enable command and signal. Wedge is suitable for open terrain where dispersion and observation are critical. Trail elements protect the rear and flank. Adjustments to the wedge are made based on visibility, terrain restrictions, and likelihood of enemy contact. Wedge is the default formation for movement to contact.

Patrol base occupation drill: leader's recon confirms suitability, then alpha team provides security while the rest of the platoon files into the position. Once inside, R&S teams emplace, claymores set, sectors of fire confirmed, range cards completed. Priority of work follows: security, weapons maintenance, personal hygiene, rest. No more than one-third of the element will be at less than full alert at any time.

Measurement and signature intelligence detected enemy activity through technical signatures: thermal, acoustic, seismic, and electromagnetic. The military intelligence brigade employed MASINT sensors along likely enemy avenues of approach. Sensor activations cued response forces or further collection to confirm enemy activity before committing kinetic engagement assets. MASINT provided persistent unattended surveillance that complemented human and signals intelligence collection across the area of operations.

Commander's critical information requirements are decomposed into PIRs for the enemy and FFIRs for friendly forces. CCIRs drive the collection and reporting plan. PIRs and FFIRs are reviewed at the daily commander's update brief and adjusted based on the operational situation. Each CCIR is owned by a staff section and has assigned indicators, NAIs, and collection assets. CCIRs not being answered are flagged for action.

Bird inbound, three mikes out. Mark LZ with VS-17 panel, orange side up. Wind from the south at five knots, indicate by smoke as the aircraft approaches. Casualty packaged on litter, IV established, fluid running TKO. Tourniquet times annotated on the forehead. Casualty card complete and stapled to the patient. Stand by for hoist ops.

Air assault planning followed the reverse planning sequence: actions on objective drove the LZ selection, the LZ selection drove the flight route, and the flight route drove the PZ time and aircraft configuration. The S3 air worked the lift requirement with the aviation task force, deconflicted airspace through the BCD, and locked in the timeline at the operations order brief. Synchronization mattered more than speed.

Illumination missions kept the night battlefield bathed in light when needed. The FO called for illumination over the suspected enemy avenue of approach. The mortar fired flares fuzed to burst at altitude and descend slowly under parachute, providing visible light for the soldiers to identify and engage targets. Burning time was approximately fifty seconds per flare. Repeat fires sustained illumination as long as the tactical situation required.

Full motion video exploitation from UAS feeds required deliberate processes to manage the volume of imagery collected. The brigade imagery exploitation cell tasked specific collection requirements, monitored live feeds for time-sensitive indicators, and archived recorded video for subsequent analysis. Pattern of life development from extended observation periods produced intelligence that single-pass collections could not. Persistent surveillance changed the intelligence collection paradigm at the tactical level.

Nine-line, nine-line, nine-line. Pickup is at grid alpha-bravo seven-seven-two-niner-zero-one. Two patients, both Cat A, one penetrating abdominal trauma, one severe head injury, both unresponsive. Hoist required, dense canopy on the X. Hostile contact possible within the last hour, recommend escort. Mark with chem light buzzsaw at night. Send. Over.

The combatant commander divided the theater into joint operations areas under subordinate joint task force commanders. Each JTF owned its AOR for all military operations within boundaries. Higher-echelon assets passed through subordinate AORs only after coordination with the battlespace owner. Coordinating altitudes separated rotary wing operations from fixed wing strike packages without requiring continuous airspace coordination during execution.

Range card for the crew-served weapon shows primary direction of fire, primary sector of fire, dead space within sector, principal direction of fire, final protective line, and TRPs. Distances and azimuths to TRPs are marked. Sector limits are physically marked with aiming stakes. Range card is filed in the position and one copy retained by the squad leader. Card is updated when weapon position is altered.

Are there any questions on this order? Time check, my time is zero-two-three-five local in three, two, one, hack. Next time hack at zero-three-hundred. Brief-back from squad leaders required NLT zero-two-five-zero. Rehearsals: full mission rehearsal at zero-three-one-zero, actions on the objective rehearsal at zero-three-three-zero. Out.

Roger your last, transmitting SITREP. Forward observer reports adjusting fires on TRP Two-Four. First round splash in three-zero seconds. Maneuver element in support by fire is set. Breach element is at the release point. We are five mikes to assault initiation. Recommend you confirm CAS holding at the IP. Acknowledge receipt. How copy, over.

Escalation of force procedures at the ECP follow a standard ladder. Shout to gain attention. Show weapons posture. Shove or use physical barriers if proximity allows. Shoot warning round into a backstop if authorized. Shoot to disable the vehicle. Shoot to kill if the driver is assessed as committing a hostile act. Each step must be documented in the post log.

CBRN reconnaissance mission requires specialized equipment and trained operators. Fox NBCRS vehicles or comparable platforms conduct mounted reconnaissance of suspected contaminated areas. Dismounted survey teams with M256 kits validate readings. Marker sets identify confirmed contamination boundaries. Findings are reported via NBC4 message to the CBRN cell at brigade. Avoidance routes are then disseminated to maneuver elements via overlay.

Post-raid AAR captures sustains, improves, and lessons learned. Each element leader contributes observations from their portion of the operation. Issues are categorized into doctrine, organization, training, materiel, leadership, personnel, facilities, and policy domains. Recommended changes feed the unit's tactics, techniques, and procedures documentation. Significant lessons are shared with adjacent units and higher headquarters.

Maritime special operations conducted boarding and clearing of vessels at sea through visit, board, search, and seizure procedures. The boarding team approached the target vessel under cover of supporting craft, embarked via hook and climb or fast-rope from helicopter, and cleared the vessel compartment by compartment. The compliant boarding procedure assumed cooperation; the opposed boarding procedure assumed resistance. Each contingency required separate training and rehearsal across the team.

Paragraph two, mission. First platoon attacks NLT zero-three-zero-zero local on six May to seize OBJ Falcon in order to enable second platoon's follow-on attack on OBJ Hawk. Paragraph three, execution. Commander's intent, key tasks, end state. Concept of the operation: support by fire, breach, assault. Tasks to subordinate units, coordinating instructions, including PIRs and CCIRs.

Backbriefs from subordinate commanders to the brigade commander confirmed understanding of the mission, the concept of the operation, and the supporting tasks. The battalion commanders briefed back their concept of how they would accomplish their portion of the operation. The brigade commander asked questions, refined guidance, and confirmed the subordinate units could execute the operation as planned. Backbriefs surfaced friction before execution.

Code word for tonight is Sierra-Mike-Oscar-Kilo-Echo, response Foxtrot-India-Romeo-Echo. Use proword 'Authenticate' only when challenging unknown callsigns. If response is incorrect or delayed beyond five seconds, assume the station is compromised and refer immediately to the duty signal officer. Codewords rotate at zero-zero-zero-one Zulu.

Counter-sniper procedures begin with deliberate analysis of likely enemy firing positions across the AO. The S2 produced a modified combined obstacle overlay marking buildings with line of sight to friendly avenues of approach. Scout sniper teams occupied dominating terrain, established sectors of observation, and maintained continuous coverage of the named areas of interest while the maneuver force conducted operations below.

Post-blast investigation procedures: secure the scene, photograph the crater and surrounding area in a methodical pattern, sketch the scene with measurements, collect fragments and components, document witnesses and observations, and transport collected material to the technical exploitation lab. Chain of custody is maintained throughout. Reporting follows the WIT format, which integrates with theater-wide IED defeat analysis.

The 120mm heavy mortar section provided the battalion commander with organic indirect fires out to seven thousand meters. The section operated in two-gun configurations, fired both high explosive and precision-guided rounds, and could displace within five minutes of last round fired. Section chiefs trained relentlessly on emplacement, firing data, and displacement to maintain the responsiveness the battalion required to support the maneuver companies.

Tank-infantry integration in restricted terrain demanded close coordination between the tank platoon and the supported rifle company. Infantry cleared dead ground that tanks couldn't observe; tanks provided direct fire support and shock action against fortified positions. Communications between dismounted infantry and the tank crew used the company net plus pyrotechnics for emergency signaling. The combined arms team multiplied capability beyond either element alone.

Priority of work in the patrol base proceeds in order: weapons and equipment maintenance, personal hygiene, water and rations consumption, rest. Each task is conducted by no more than one-third of the element at a time, the remainder maintaining security. Squad leaders supervise the work cycle and ensure all critical tasks are completed before the platoon transitions to the next phase.

AAR ground rules include no rank or position in the room, candid input from all participants, focus on what happened not who did it, and confidentiality of personal observations outside the AAR. The goal is unit improvement, not assignment of blame. When ground rules are honored, soldiers contribute openly and the unit grows from the experience. When violated, the AAR becomes a formality and learning suffers.

Counter-mobility operations slowed and shaped the enemy with obstacle effects while the brigade attacked or defended. The engineer commander coordinated counter-mobility with mobility operations on friendly avenues of approach. Friendly mobility required obstacle reduction, route clearance, and bridge construction; counter-mobility required obstacle emplacement, minefield seeding, and demolitions against avenues of approach the enemy might use. Engineers balanced both requirements within available resources.

Counterattack by the battalion reserve restored the integrity of the defense if enemy forces penetrated the main battle area. The reserve held in a defilade assembly area, rehearsed multiple counterattack options, and stayed mounted and ready for commitment on the battalion commander's order. Counterattack timing balanced the need to restore the line against preservation of the reserve for subsequent contingencies during the defense.

Class nine repair parts kept brigade equipment operational across sustained operations. The maintenance company tracked parts requisitions through the standard army management information system, expedited critical items through the corps logistics support element, and managed the brigade parts inventory at the brigade support area. Operational readiness rates reflected parts availability as much as maintenance team capacity throughout extended deployments to contested operational environments.

Right two-zero, add five-zero, repeat. Effects on target observed, enemy element neutralized, estimated seventy percent casualties to the target. Cease fire, cease fire. End of mission. Surveillance, two enemy KIA, multiple WIA observed displacing east toward the wood line. Request shift to TRP Seven for follow-on suppression as they move. Over.

Running estimate maintained by each staff section integrates MOPs and MOEs into a continuously updated picture of operations. The G-3 running estimate tracks force disposition and operational tempo. The G-2 running estimate tracks enemy situation and trends. The G-4 running estimate tracks sustainment posture. Each estimate feeds the commander's daily and weekly assessment battle rhythm.

Receiving facility is Role Two Whiskey-Tango. Aircraft is Dustoff Two-Five, callsign Dustoff Two-Five. Inbound to LZ Mike, ETA four mikes. Confirm patient packaged, sensitive items consolidated, weapons cleared and tagged. Notify gaining medical officer of MIST report en route on freq Bravo. Out.

IED detonation on lead vehicle of the convoy. Immediate actions: stop convoy outside the kill zone, establish three-sixty security, identify casualties and damaged vehicles, call up nine-line MEDEVAC if required, establish blocking positions on potential secondary device locations. EOD requested via higher. Do not move from cover until route is cleared. Press reporters and noncombatants in the area held at a distance.

Governance support helped local government function effectively after security conditions improved enough to permit civilian administration. The civil affairs team partnered with district government offices, mentored officials through routine activities, and connected local government to provincial and national authorities. Governance development moved at the speed of trust between officials and population, not at the pace of military planning timelines or operational tempo.

Decisive action training scenarios combined offensive, defensive, stability, and support operations within a single exercise framework. The brigade transitioned between operational phases as the exercise scenario evolved, requiring agility across the full range of military operations. Staff planners worked multiple simultaneous problems while maneuver units executed combined arms operations under fire. The complexity replicated actual operational tempo encountered in deployment to contested areas of responsibility.

Risk assessment for the raid identifies threats to mission accomplishment and to the force. Threats are categorized by likelihood and severity, then assigned mitigations. Common mitigations include rehearsals, pre-combat checks and inspections, redundancy in critical systems, contingency planning, and on-call enabler support such as CAS, MEDEVAC, and indirect fires. Residual risk is briefed to the approving authority.
